hypothesis.text: Observable community-structure conditions — local ownership density, farm and business structure, local banking, healthcare access, journalism presence, education pathways, and demographic stability — consistently co-vary with civic engagement patterns (turnout level, stability, and persistence) such that certain environments produce more durable participation than others; identifying which variables travel together is a prerequisite for testing HYP-125/126/127 without misattributing outcomes to single instruments (campaign finance rules, civic-commons design, or voting age).
hypothesis.central_question: What conditions consistently correlate with civic engagement, participation, trust, and community durability?
hypothesis.constitutional_capitalism_test: Can Constitutional Capitalism measure how economic ownership, local institutions, information, and healthcare access travel together with civic participation — descriptively first — so later reform hypotheses are tested against community structure rather than slogans?
hypothesis.scope: Arkansas counties first (descriptive layer); national/comparative later

governance.reason: Steve-directed opening of a connective empirical track linking already-built structure systems to historic voting participation. Descriptive first. Not a baseline metric. Not a causal model at registration.

unifying_culture_question: How do we create a culture where citizens believe self-government is something they do, not something they watch?

epistemic_walls.rule: Descriptive co-variation first; no single-variable causation claims from county cross-sections.
Turnout ≠ trust ≠ volunteerism ≠ resilience. Measure separately when possible.
A county at stable 68% differs from one oscillating 25–70%. Track level, volatility, and persistence.
Ownership/concentration overlays remain relationship evidence — not automatic capture or monopsony proofs (CC-CLAIM-003 hold).
Any Community Health Index is exploratory modeling — not a National Baseline scoreboard slot.
Adult civic-structure baselines must be known before attributing Maryland/Newark/Takoma outcomes to voting age alone.

layer_1_voting_participation.time_span_target: 2000–2024 even-year cycles (and odd-year local where available)

layer_3_community_health_index.purpose: Ask which variables travel together; illustrative county sketches only until measurement dataset exists

example_sketch_only.sketch: High turnout / high growth / moderate farm density / newspaper present / high bank branches → thriving (illustrative, not measured)
Low turnout / flat pop / moderate farm / weak newspaper / low banks → struggling (illustrative, not measured)
Medium turnout / growing / strong farm / moderate newspaper / moderate banks → stable (illustrative, not measured)

layer_4_hyp126_test_surface.question: What environments produce participation?
layer_4_hyp126_test_surface.testable_contrast: Counties with stronger local ownership, local media, civic organizations, and locally controlled institutions vs weaker — compare turnout level, stability, persistence

layer_5_hyp127_control_surface.question: What baseline civic conditions produce participation among adults?
layer_5_hyp127_control_surface.rule: Use as control context before attributing youth-suffrage case outcomes to voting age alone

research_questions: What conditions appear before civic decline?
What conditions appear before civic renewal?
